newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen, Preussag plan joint shipbuilding - paper.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen, Preussag plan joint shipbuilding - paper.

text.p: A German newspaper reported on Thursday that the shipbuilding operations of Thyssen Industrie AG and Preussag AG were to work together and could eventually merge.
In an advance release from Friday's edition, the Hamburger Abendblatt daily said the two companies would begin formal talks on cooperation in the next few weeks.
"The aim is an intensive form of cooperation, up to a change in the relations of ownership," the paper quoted Thyssen Industrie spokesman Alfred Wewers as saying.

It said Thyssen Industrie chairman Eckhard Rohkamm had not ruled out a merger. A merged company would be the biggest shipbuilder in Germany with 6,500 workers and a turnover of around 3.5 billion marks, the paper said.
Under the plan, Thyssen's Blohm & Voss yard in Hamburg and its Nordseewerke yard in Emden would work together with Preussag's Howaldtswerke in Kiel, according to the newspaper.
Thyssen Industrie is the capital goods unit of Thyssen AG.
Blohm & Voss made heavy losses in 1995-96 but the Hamburger Abendblatt quoted the shipbuilder's works council chairman, Otto Tetau, as predicting a profit this year.
"Blohm & Voss will be in the black this year," he said.
